context: Data visualization — a split violin plot matrix showing daily temperature distributions across 6 cities and 12 months, comparing 2010s vs 2020s decades
first_impression: Clean grid layout with a deliberately accessible color palette, but Singapore's row collapses into flat horizontal lines and the violins are uniformly small across all cells, undermining the distribution encoding.
what_works: The Tol Bright blue/rose palette is a deliberate, colorblind-friendly choice that communicates the decade comparison clearly without feeling like a D3 default. Title/subtitle hierarchy is confident, and the light cell borders and gridlines keep chrome from competing with the data.
what_doesnt: Singapore's row is effectively unreadable — the shared y-scale compresses its narrow tropical variance (~1.5°C amplitude) into near-invisible horizontal dashes, breaking the data encoding for an entire row. The violins across all cells are also small enough that distribution shape details (tails, skew) are hard to read, and the white median lines are barely distinguishable from the violin fills at this render size.
